sense: similar to, in the manner of

terms.grammar: adverbs of comparison; the noun after them takes the case of the word it is compared with
evidence: Cic. Sen. 44: hominēs capiantur ut piscēs
terms.comment: The plain “like” of a comparison: ut piscēs, like fish.

terms.grammar: adverbs of comparison; before a clause, with the subjunctive (“as if”)
evidence: Cic. Att. 8.14.2: ego tēcum tamquam mēcum loquor

terms.gloss: like, as big as, the size of
terms.comment: Properly “the likeness, the size”: īnstar montis, as big as a mountain.

terms.grammar: adjective, third declension, with the genitive or the dative
terms.comment: When “like” follows be or look; see similar. Unlike: dissimilis (see different).

phrases.latin: dīvīnē enim Platō ‘ēscam malōrum’ appellat voluptātem, quod eā vidēlicet hominēs capiantur ut piscēs
phrases.english: for Plato, inspired, calls pleasure “the bait of evils”, because men are caught by it like fish
I talk to you as I talk to myself

phrases.latin: puerī īnstar bimulī tremulā patris dormientis in ulnā
phrases.english: like a little boy of two asleep in his father’s rocking arm

phrases.latin: tum sēmen seritō crēbrum tamquam līnum, eō terram crībrō incernitō altam digitum trānsversum
phrases.english: then sow the seed thick, like flax, and sift earth over it a finger’s breadth deep

phrases.latin: mūtāta omnia altōque cinere tamquam nive obducta
phrases.english: everything was changed, and covered in deep ash, as if with snow

phrases.latin: nōlī, inquit, tamquam assem elephantō dēs
phrases.english: “Don’t hold it out,” he said, “as if you were giving a penny to an elephant”

phrases.latin: similis erit virō stultō, quī aedificāvit domum suam super arēnam
phrases.english: he will be like a foolish man who built his house upon the sand
